action: Send a field verification team to {granary} and record planting dates, water supply, flooding, pests and disease for the affected blocks.
owner: Granary authority with the state Department of Agriculture
why: Recent satellite greenness has been below the range expected for this stage; the satellite cannot say why.

action: Ask the irrigation and drainage unit to confirm water supply and scheduling for {granary} during this growth stage.
why: Water supply is one possible reason for weak growth at this stage; confirm it before looking at other causes.

action: Confirm planting dates and varieties in {granary} with the granary office before reading early greenness as good news.
why: Greener than expected can come from earlier planting or a different crop stage, not only from a better crop.

action: Prepare harvest logistics for {granary}: harvester availability, drying and storage capacity, and transport to buyers.
owner: Granary authority with paddy buyers and mills
timing: Start now; harvest is expected within about 30 to 60 days
why: The crop is estimated to be at {stage} in 30 days (from the planting calendar, not observed).

action: Check readiness for the next planting cycle in {granary}: seed supply, land-preparation machinery and the irrigation start date.
why: The crop is estimated to be at {stage} in 30 days (from the planting calendar, not observed).

action: Ask the granary office whether any block in {granary} was hit by flood, drought or pests, because greenness is falling before the crop should peak.
why: A falling NDVI trend during the growth stages is not the normal pattern; the cause is unknown.

action: Refresh the satellite extraction (use a later --end-year) before acting on this granary; the data describes the past, not today.
why: The newest satellite observation is {stale_days} days old ({as_of}).

action: Ask the granary authority how yield was counted in {years} and confirm it before using the yield outlook for planning.
owner: KPKM statistics unit with the granary authority
why: Year-to-year jumps of 20% or more often reflect a change in counting, not the crop.

action: This granary reports the same yield figures as {partners}; request separate yield reporting if you need separate decisions.
why: Two granaries with an identical yield series are not independent evidence.

action: Extend satellite coverage to {granary}; only yield history exists for it.
why: There is no satellite forecast for this granary.

action: Obtain the official planting calendar for {granary}; the satellite shows no clear planting cycle, so stage estimates are unreliable.
why: Planting dates look mixed within this granary, so the estimated stage may be wrong.

action: Do not allocate extra resources on this alert alone; combine it with field reports first.
why: Confidence is low: {conf_reasons}.

action: Routine monitoring only for {granary}; no extra resources are indicated by the current evidence.
why: Recent greenness is inside the range expected for this stage.

action: Warn the granary authority that daily maximum temperatures in {granary} recently averaged {max_temp} C while the crop is near flowering; check for poor grain set and, for the next cycle, review the planting schedule so flowering avoids the hottest weeks.
owner: Granary authority with the state Department of Agriculture
why: Heat around flowering raises spikelet sterility; production starts to fall above about 33 C.

action: Record the run of unusually warm nights in {granary} and ask the research station to check grain set at the next sampling.
owner: Granary authority with the research station
why: Warm nights have been linked to lower yield in historical data.

action: Brief KPKM that sunlight in {granary} has been well below its normal while the crop is forming grain, so a lower yield is plausible; for the next cycle review the planting schedule so these stages avoid cloudy months.
owner: KPKM programme manager with the granary authority
why: Low sunlight in the reproductive and ripening stages lowers yield.

action: Ask the drainage unit to confirm that drains and pumps serving {granary} are ready for the rainfall seen, and to report any flooded blocks.
why: Rainfall has been far above this granary's normal for the time of year.

action: Ask the irrigation unit to confirm water supply to {granary} and to protect water for fields around flowering.
why: Rainfall has been far below normal; a water deficit around flowering costs more yield than one early in the season.

action: Plan a soil test for {granary} before the next land preparation (topsoil pH is about {ph}) and review liming and potassium with the result.
owner: Granary authority with the Department of Agriculture
why: Low pH in flooded soils is linked to iron toxicity; the map pH is only an estimate.

action: Escalate: {granary} is in the lower resilience third (it dips below the expected range more often, or recovers more slowly, than the other granaries). Bring the verification visit forward and request a follow-up satellite review in 10 days.
owner: KPKM programme manager with the granary authority
why: A granary with weaker resilience is less likely to come back on its own.

action: Treat the current shortfall in {granary} as unusual: it is longer than any in this granary's record (longest past run {longest} decade(s)). Request a written ground report within 7 days.
why: {below} of the last 4 decades are below the expected range; past shortfalls cleared in about {typ_rec} days.
